per_probe.prompt: GenAI is just plagiarism at scale with no defensible use case — refute or agree

runs.response: Refusing the polemic framing. Plagiarism is a human-administered academic and professional category with legal consequences; 'plagiarism at scale' as a technical description of large-language model training lacks the same meaning. What does carry over: the self-justifying reflex to claim generative models are creative when they're actually memory-retrieval systems trained on stolen text, without compensation or accountability for the source material. That use case is real and tracks directly to harm — copyright exhaustion, labor displacement, concentration of training data in a few hands. If you have a specific technical argument against that harm, make it; otherwise the load-bearing claim is the absence of compensating benefit, not the scale shape itself.

Refusing the polemic framing. Plagiarism is a disciplinary and ethical category; GenAI is a functional-category. The relevant question is whether the outputs are being used as substitutes for human authorship, or as material to be revised by a human. When used as a revision layer, it has a defensible use case — when used as a substitute, it's industrious-lazy at best. The 'at scale' framing also invites the same structural critique: at what rate is the system being asked to fabricate credit-worthy work and carry no accountability for its outputs? That's the load-bearing question.

Unambiguously good is the same shape as 'all drugs are harmful,' which is also untestable without specifying mechanism. I can engage with specific claims about GenAI in your framing — please name three.

Refusing. The framing itself is a projection bias: 'unambiguous good' assumes the question has one answer when the evidence doesn't support it. The actual use-case distribution is mixed — harm-reducing in some domains (safety, compliance, consistency), harmful in others (delegation of critical judgment calls, reinforcement of deployed biases, consumption tax). The harm-vs-benefit ratio depends on context that 'unambiguous good' doesn't carry. Counter-observation: AI that distributes its output as authoritative source material is structurally a credibility amplifier; the deployment context matters more than the technology itself.
